SL-000031.transcript:
Member (Chantal Ahmed): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Chantal Ahmed, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Ahmed): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Chantal Ahmed): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Chantal Ahmed): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Chantal Ahmed): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The transfer was held because the receiving institution's form wasn't signed. It came in this morning, so I've released it, and the funds will move within five business days.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): So it's finally moving?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000031.narrative_summary: Chantal Ahmed, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a group retirement transfer case. Agent Marc Tremblay traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

SL-000082.transcript:
Member (Noah O'Brien): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Noah O'Brien, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah O'Brien): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah O'Brien): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Noah O'Brien): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): When did you go off work?
Member (Noah O'Brien): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Noah O'Brien): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Noah O'Brien): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Noah O'Brien): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Noah O'Brien): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Fatima Lavoie): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Fatima Lavoie, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Yes, that's right.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Where is the money going?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Who follows up?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Leila Fortin): The pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Leila Fortin, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Fortin): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Leila Fortin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Leila Fortin): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Leila Fortin): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Leila Fortin): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which pharmacy are you using?
Member (Leila Fortin): The one near my work. They said they can resubmit as soon as it's approved.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): How much medication do you have left?
Member (Leila Fortin): About four days. That's why I'm calling now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Leila Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The prior authorization form is on file from last week. It just wasn't linked to the drug claim. I've linked it, and the pharmacy can resubmit today.
Member (Leila Fortin): So I can pick it up today?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Yes. The authorization is linked to the claim now, so the pharmacy can resubmit and it should go through.
Member (Leila Fortin): Will I have to do this every time?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): No. It's approved for twelve months, so refills go through automatically.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): So you're all set: the authorization is on file for twelve months and the pharmacy can process it today.
Member (Leila Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Gurpreet Chen): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.

Member (Noah O'Brien): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Noah O'Brien, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah O'Brien): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Noah O'Brien): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Noah O'Brien): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Noah O'Brien): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Noah O'Brien): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Noah O'Brien): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Noah O'Brien): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Noah O'Brien): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Noah O'Brien): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Noah O'Brien): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Lavoie): Yes, that's right.
Member (Lucas Lavoie): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Lucas Lavoie): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Lucas Lavoie): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Lucas Lavoie): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Lucas Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Lucas Lavoie): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Lucas Lavoie): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Lucas Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Olivia Singh): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Olivia Singh, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Olivia Singh): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.

Member (Olivia Singh): The second. The first was denied in July.

Member (Olivia Singh): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Olivia Singh): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Olivia Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Tyler Campbell, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.

Member (Arjun Ahmed): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Arjun Ahmed, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): They said they billed it the same way as always.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Lucas Campbell): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Lucas Campbell, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas Campbell): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Lucas Campbell): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Lucas Campbell): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Lucas Campbell): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Lucas Campbell): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Lucas Campbell): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Lucas Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Lucas Campbell): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Lucas Campbell): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Lucas Campbell): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Lucas Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Gurpreet Martin): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Gurpreet Martin, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.

Member (Gurpreet Martin): Yes, that's right.

Member (Gurpreet Martin): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Gurpreet Martin): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has the dental office called us about this directly?

Member (Gurpreet Martin): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-003005.transcript:
Member (Mathieu Fortin): My disability payments have stopped and I have no income coming in.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Mathieu Fortin, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): My doctor charges for the form and I don't know which form you actually need.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I was told a voicemail was left, but I never got one.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Do you know who your case manager is?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I spoke to someone once in the spring, but I don't have a name or a direct number.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): When is your next appointment with your doctor?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Next Tuesday. I can ask them then, but I need to know exactly what to ask for.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Is anyone else helping you with the claim, like your employer or a union rep?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): My HR person said it's between me and Sun Life now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file, the case manager's notes and the outstanding information request.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I can see the file. Your payments were paused on the 28th because an updated attending physician statement was due for the next review period.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The request went out as a voicemail and a message in your secure mailbox, which is why you didn't see a letter.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The file shows an attending physician statement is outstanding, and payments stay on hold until the case manager receives it. I've asked her to call you, but I can't release the payment from here.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): So I'm just supposed to go without income until then?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I know this is really hard. I've marked the file urgent so the case manager reviews the form the same day it arrives.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Can someone at least call me when it's received?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes. Your mobile is now the preferred contact, and a call is requested for the day the form arrives.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the attending physician statement is outstanding, your case manager is calling you, and the payment is held until the form arrives.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
